subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs — alignment & next steps
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elenap@medicore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T16:10:00Z
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs — alignment & next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap below so we have a shared starting point and clear next steps. Please correct anything I’ve misstated.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Token costs from current OpenAI/Anthropic usage are volatile and account for ~40% of feature costs; need 25–35% reduction target to be economical.
- Latency spikes in peak hours (current 300–800ms tail) are affecting UX for chat and agent flows.
- Vendor lock-in and lack of on-prem/network isolation for regulated patient data.
- Procurement wants SOC 2 evidence and KMS/HSM support before any POC.

Current stack (what you said)
- Chat & completion: OpenAI (gpt-4o) as primary with fallback to Anthropic for safety-sensitive flows.
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small at ~250k requests/month.
- Inference hosted in us-west region (multi-tenant).
- Minimal internal tooling for quantized model hosting — most of ops is vendor-managed.

Success criteria for a migration/POC
- Output parity: human-evaluated answer quality within a 10–15% gap on our core prompt set.
- Latency: median within 15% and P95 under 700ms for chat path at expected traffic.
- Cost: net token/unit cost reduction target 30%+ for steady-state.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration, and option for VPC/private deployment.

Preliminary model shortlist (based on compatibility needs you listed)
- Llama-3 70B (quantized 4-bit) — promising on cost, requires sampling/temperature tuning.
- Mistral Instruct family — strong instruction-following; test for hallucination profile.
- RedPajama-INC or community-instructed 33B variants — lighter footprint for embeddings/short completion tasks.

Compatibility & API feature needs (must-have for POC)
- Streaming token output + chunked responses for progressive UI rendering.
- Function-calling / structured JSON output for our QA pipeline.
- Embeddings API parity (same dims and semantic drift tolerance).
- Rate-limits and retry behavior configurable to match existing client SDKs.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Share sample prompt set and 48-hour representative traffic snapshot (you agreed to send).
2) Tech deep-dive (1hr) with your infra/security + our infra lead (Aditya) and solutions lead (Ben) — propose times below.
3) Redwood to share migration outline + sample prompt-set attached.
4) If security checks look good, schedule a 6-week POC: week 0 onboarding, weeks 1–3 evaluation, weeks 4–6 optimization and QoE testing.

Proposed times for the technical deep-dive (PT):
- Wed 2027-05-12, 10:00–11:00 PT
- Thu 2027-05-13, 13:00–14:00 PT
- Mon 2027-05-17, 09:00–10:00 PT

Docs attached: redwood-migration-outline.pdf (POC plan + data handling), sample-prompt-set.json (anonymized). HubSpot record and calendar link below.

If this looks right, I’ll loop in Aditya and Ben on the calendar invite and include our security pack (SOC2 + KMS notes).

Thanks — Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
maya.srinivasan@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

---
Attachment: redwood-migration-outline.pdf (PDF, 18KB)
Attachment: sample-prompt-set.json (JSON, 6KB)
From: Elena Park <elenap@medicore.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@medicore.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T18:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs — alignment & next steps

Thanks Maya — this is great and captures the conversation well. A few clarifications from our side:

- Monthly footprint: ~6M generated tokens (chat/completions) and ~250k embedding calls. Peak concurrency around 120–150 rps during business hours.
- Latency target: aim for median under 350ms and P95 < 700ms for the chat path.
- Procurement checklist: beyond SOC 2 and KMS, we’ll need encryption-at-rest details, proof of regional hosting (US-only for PHI-related flows), and an IP/data segregation statement.
- Our security lead (Rajiv, cc’d) will want the SOC2 report and any pen-test summary before a POC kickoff.

We can get the anonymized prompt set and a 48-hour traffic dump to you by EOD Friday. For the tech deep-dive, Thu 2027-05-13, 13:00 PT works for us.

One more ask: can Redwood confirm whether you support streaming + function/call semantics that are wire-compatible with our current SDKs? If there are API differences, we’ll need a short migration map.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Elena
Elena Park
Director of AI Product, Medicore Health
elenap@medicore.com | +1 (212) 555-3390
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elenap@medicore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs — alignment & next steps

Elena / Rajiv — thanks for the clarifications and for confirming Thu 5/13 at 13:00 PT. I’ve penciled it in and will send a calendar invite once Aditya confirms availability (cc’d).

Quick answers to the two asks:
- Streaming & function-calls: Redwood supports streaming token output and a function-calling pattern that is compatible at the wire level with the majority of OpenAI/Anthropic client SDKs. There are minor differences in our field names (we’ll include a 1-page migration map in the POC packet).
- Security pack: Ben will attach the SOC 2 summary and KMS integration notes to the invite. We also provide an IP/data segregation statement and options for a VPC-private control plane for regulated workloads.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Aditya + Ben to join Thu 2027-05-13, 13:00 PT deep-dive.
2) Elena to send anonymized prompt set + 48h traffic snapshot by EOD Friday.
3) Redwood to circulate SOC2 + KMS docs + 1-page API migration map prior to the call.
4) Post-call: agree on POC scope and sign mutual NDA if needed (we can send a simple one-pager).

Proposed meeting invite description: 60m Technical deep-dive | Redwood (Aditya, Ben) + Medicore (Elena, Rajiv) — focus: latency profile, streaming & function-call parity, security gating.

Anything to add? If not, we’ll lock Thu and I’ll send the invite.

Best — Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
maya.srinivasan@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182
